ei.title: Young Enough to Change the World

fullPassage:
Young Enough to Change the World

Many young people are making the world a better place. For example, Carter and Olivia Ries have become leaders in saving animals. Although they are only teenagers, they have actually made a difference in the world. How were they able to do that? Let's hear from Carter.

When I was five, my little sister Olivia and I each adopted a cheetah. Did we raise cheetahs at home? No, we donated to a charity that protects wild cheetahs in South Africa. Our parents told us that if we did not protect them, we might not be able to see cheetahs in the near future. We soon became interested in helping other endangered animals. A few years later, with help from our parents, we created a non-profit organization to protect them. We wanted the next generation to be able to see these animals, so we named our organization One More Generation. We also studied endangered animals and educated our friends about them.

Then one day, a terrible oil spill occurred in the Gulf of Mexico. A lot of sea animals were completely covered with oil, and they were dying. We had to do something. We started collecting animal rescue supplies such as pet carrying cages and rubber gloves from everyone in our neighborhood. Four months later, our family drove to the Gulf of Mexico to deliver what we collected and helped to save the animals. While we were working there, we learned something very useful. When we put mayonnaise into a turtle's throat, the turtle threw up. That way, we were able to get oil out of turtles. I never knew mayonnaise could be used to save animals!

On our last day, we met a marine life specialist. She told us that plastic waste is more dangerous to sea animals than oil spills are. A lot of sea animals and sea birds die from eating plastic waste. After we came home, we created an educational project about how to reduce plastic waste. In addition to this, our organization continues to do various projects to save animals. Although we started small, we are making a big difference. What you do today can change the world, so take that first step!

questions.stem:
주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

When I was five, my little sister Olivia and I each adopted a cheetah.

(A) We soon became interested in helping other endangered animals.
(B) No, we donated to a charity that protects wild cheetahs in South Africa.
(C) Our parents told us that if we did not protect them, we might not be able to see cheetahs in the near future.

det.analysis:
✅ ④ (B)-(C)-(A): 입양 → 기부 설명(B) → 보호 필요(C) → 관심 확대(A).
❌ ① (A) 먼저는 기부 설명 없이 관심 확대 — 비논리적.
❌ ② (C) 먼저면 경고가 기부 설명보다 먼저 — 부자연.
❌ ③ (C) 먼저면 기부 설명 없이 경고.

questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 올바르게 배열한 것은?
"비록 그들은 십 대일 뿐이지만, 세상에 변화를 일으켜 왔다."
[although / made a difference / they are only teenagers / they have actually / in the world]
ch: They have actually although they are only teenagers made a difference in the world
They are only teenagers although they have actually made a difference in the world
Although they are only teenagers, they have actually made a difference in the world
Although made a difference they are only teenagers, they have actually in the world

det.korean: 비록 십 대이지만, 세상에 변화를 일으켰다.

❌ ② although 위치 잘못.

❌ ④ although가 중간에 오면 의미 달라짐.
det.tip: Although + 양보절, 주절. although절이 앞에 오면 콤마(,) 구분.

"우리는 다음 세대가 이러한 동물들을 볼 수 있기를 원했다."
[the next generation / wanted / to be able to / we / see these animals]
ch: We the next generation wanted to be able to see these animals
We wanted the next generation to be able to see these animals
We wanted see these animals to be able to the next generation
We wanted to be able to the next generation see these animals

det.korean: 우리는 다음 세대가 동물을 볼 수 있기를 원했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② want+목적어+to부정사 올바른 어순.
❌ ① to be able to 위치 잘못.
❌ ④ the next generation 위치 잘못.
❌ ③ see these animals 위치 잘못.

questions.passage: No, we donated to a charity (A)[that / what] protects wild cheetahs in South Africa. Our parents told us that if we did not protect them, we might not be able to see cheetahs in the near future. We wanted the next generation (B)[seeing / to see] these animals.
questions.stem: (A)와 (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 치타를 보호하는 자선단체. 동물을 볼 수 있기를 원했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ that — to see:
(A) that: 선행사 a charity가 있으므로 관계대명사 that.
(B) to see: want+O+to V 구조.
❌ ② what: 선행사 있으면 불가.
❌ ③ seeing: want+O+to V.
❌ ① 둘 다 틀림.

questions.passage: Four months later, our family drove to the Gulf of Mexico to deliver (A)[that / what] we collected. While we were working there, we learned something very useful. I never knew mayonnaise could (B)[be used / use] to save animals!
questions.stem: (A)와 (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 모은 것을 전달하기 위해. 사용될 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① what — be used:
(A) what: 선행사 없이 명사절.
(B) be used: 수동태 필요.
❌ ② that: 선행사 없으므로 불가.
❌ ③ use: 능동태 부적절.
❌ ④ that: 불가.
det.tip: what(선행사 포함) vs that(선행사 필요). be used to+V(수동).

questions.passage: ①<u>Although</u> we started small, we are making a big difference. ②<u>What</u> you do today can change the world, ③<u>so</u> take that first step! Many young people ④<u>is making</u> the world a better place.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ①Although: 양보 접속사 적절.
✅ ②What: 관계대명사 what 적절.
✅ ③so: 결과 접속사 적절.
❌ ④is making: 주어 Many young people은 복수 → are making.

questions.passage: Many young people are making the world a better place. For example, Carter and Olivia Ries have become leaders in saving animals. Although they are only teenagers, they have actually made a ①<u>difference</u> in the world. When I was five, my little sister Olivia and I each ②<u>adopted</u> a cheetah. No, we donated to a charity that ③<u>destroys</u> wild cheetahs in South Africa. Our parents told us that if we did not protect them, we might not be able to see cheetahs in the ④<u>near</u> future.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ①difference: 변화를 일으키다 적절.
✅ ②adopted: 입양했다 적절.
❌ ③destroys: 원문은 'protects(보호하다)'. 자선단체가 치타를 '파괴'하는 것은 반대.
✅ ④near: 가까운 미래 적절.
